guard: the out-of-band remedy a user-mesh refusal prints is a NARROW grant, spelled out field by field, rather than a bare verb whose omitted flags mean the wide default
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/manager build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/auth build && pnpm smoke:user-spawn:live
why: A confinement refusal lends its own authority to whatever command it prints, and this half of
this one printed a bare `cotal actor grant`. `runActor` fills every omitted flag from
`csv(values.x, dflt)` with the WIDE default: `>` read, `>` post, `spawn,role:default` scope. So an
operator following a refusal in order to grant a READER of one event plane wrote a row that reads
and posts on every channel in the space and can spawn, which is strictly worse than the spawn the
refusal blocked, and it arrives carrying the manager's authority.
A security lens found it after the static half of the same sentence was fixed. The cells parse the
command out of the refusal and run the values it printed through the real ledger writer, so the
text and the row cannot drift apart. R1 reverts the text to the bare verb.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite loads the manager from `implementations/manager/dist/index.js`, so
the command builds the manager before running and `afterRestore` rebuilds it, or a restored source
would sit behind a mutated dist and every later run would grade the wrong tree.

mutations.name: R1 the user-mesh refusal prints a bare actor grant, whose omitted flags mean the wide default
mutations.expectRed: the user-mesh refusal prints an actor grant that spells out EVERY field, so no wide default applies

mutations.note: This is the shipped state of the text until a security lens read it against `runActor`'s defaults. The second cell reddens too, because the parsed flags fall back to `>` and the row that lands is the wide one an operator would have written.
